license.notes: Authored 2026-09-16 for Zoo 1.0.0 from the walker's own photograph of a 1990s electronic cash register, described in core/register_forms.py. Construction knowledge only: no manufacturer, no model, no moulded badge and no sticker from that photograph reaches the tools. The only strings the species paints are a price in digits and the word TOTAL, and a denylist test holds both against core/card_brands.py's list of real marks.

notes: A 1997 electronic cash register: a squat moulded body on a deeper cash drawer, a raised customer display on a short post carrying green type on a black screen, a reflective green operator panel angled at the clerk, a receipt printer with a curl of paper in it and a painted keypad in a raised well. BEVEL IS 0 IN EVERY STYLE and that is the point of the budget: no primitive asks for one, so the module ships the 134 triangles core/register_forms.triangles counts, at every one of the 27 genome corners. tris_lod0 is register_forms.TRI_BUDGET and the two are held equal by a test. THE CUSTOMER DISPLAY IS EMISSIVE AND IS NOT A LIGHT: params.lit 0 is a register with its plug pulled (the same switch vending_machine has had since 0.87.0), and nothing in the recipe spawns a Light3D -- GL Compatibility allows 8 lights on one mesh and the card-shop package already ships 84. Front (-Y) is the CUSTOMER side, so the operator stands at +Y and the keypad sits on the -X half of the top, which is that operator's right hand.
